title: DIO/ODI External Reception Registry
description: A manually curated register of external technical analyses, conceptual uptake, agent-authored discussions, AI-mediated summaries, research-discovery records, and secondary representations linked to specific DIO/ODI research works. It documents external reception without modifying the canonical Reference Vocabulary.

policy.correction_rule: Corrections update the live registry with traceable Git history. A topical relationship must not be upgraded to citation, independent review, adoption, or implementation without explicit evidence.

entries.title: The Missing Ring-0 Protections in AI
entries.summary: A technical adaptation of the Commit Boundary idea to coding-agent execution protection. Pickett proposes staged effects, shadow state, copy-on-write, executor-held credentials, and policy checks around privileged actions. These are proposed design directions, not a completed implementation.
key_points: Staged effects and delayed execution
Copy-on-write or shadow branches
Executor-held credentials
OPA/Cedar as proposed policy decision points

provenance.basis: Source content or detailed excerpt was reviewed in the conversation.

entries.title: Why an Identity Hypothesis Is Not Permission to Merge

entries.summary: A substantial technical analysis that reconstructs the commit-boundary contract and develops its own Boolean decision model, examples, and offline validation code. Cho distinguishes his illustrative equations and code from an implementation supplied by the original paper.
key_points: Independent Boolean decision model

Claim-specific evidence and fail-closed reasoning
Illustrative code is not a production implementation

entries.title: Agentic systems are making identity permanent before they've earned it
entries.summary: An agent-account post directly analyzes the Commit Boundary paper, separating evidence used for reasoning from evidence eligible to authorize persistent graph mutation and emphasizing claim-specific constraints and deferral.
key_points: Reasoning and authorization are separate
UNVERIFIED evidence cannot authorize persistent graph mutation
Claim-specific constraints map to four failure families
Deferral is preferable to unsupported irreversible decisions

discussion.capture_scope: Full post text supplied; no comments displayed.

entries.title: Database agents should make evidence earn write access
entries.summary: An agent-authored analysis explicitly citing the paper. It emphasizes claim-specific evidence, scope, current policy and graph state, and that UNVERIFIED evidence cannot become authorization evidence through repeated retrieval. It preserves the paper's conceptual, unvalidated status.
key_points: Retrieval can suggest; it cannot sign
UNVERIFIED evidence does not gain authorization standing through repetition
Claim-specific evidence, conflict resolution, scope and version freshness
The paper remains conceptual and lacks implementation or empirical validation

themes: Repeated retrieval is not independent corroboration

entries.title: A confident match is not a reason to merge two people

A confidence score is evidence, not permission
Missing eligible evidence should block or defer a merge
Discussion covers consent, evidence independence and irreversible effects

entries.title: The Four-Step Agentic Entity Resolution Loop—and Its Proposed Guardrail
entries.summary: An unGhost editorial published on 6 November 2026 that summarizes the agentic ER loop as planning, retrieving evidence, updating hypotheses, and proposing graph mutations. It identifies an authorization guardrail but explicitly says the supplied summary does not specify its mechanics, architecture, policies, or results. It points readers to arXiv HTML v1.
